hub.scope: Hub at / only. Prints in The Late City Edition since 2026-10-31; these entries record only where it differs or adds. Mumbai Key Art is retired (owner, 2026-10-31).
hub.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Front Page"**

The network map is the front page, and every line has a printed record. The reader sees every metro line in the region on the real map, by stage, picks a line, and reads its record in a ruled fact box beside the map, each figure with its grade and source. Below: the register of every line by work stage, the latest updates, where the lines meet, the colophon. The hub adds the bundle: one stroke per primary line colour, across the top and down the left, carrying each section at a stop.
keyCharacteristics: Newsprint and navy editions, Anek 75% 800 heads, Mukta copy, 4px ink rules and 1px column rules; no cards, no shadows.
Ink masthead band (navy on morning paper, cream on night), edition line, Inside index of four sections; under 30rem the Inside list wraps.

The bundle: one 4px stroke per primary line with a sourced colour, network.json order, each colour once (branches share their primary's stroke; 8 strokes today, Lines 1 to 8), 6px pitch; --tw, --bend and --stops computed in index.astro as desktop px times --k; bend, left run and paper capsule stops on every screen (--k 0.5 and --tg 1rem under 64rem).
The front: map minmax(0, 1fr) and fact box minmax(22rem, 30rem), height max(30rem, 100svh - 22rem), ending at the fold at 1440 by 900.
Map: static drawing painted at once, MapLibre fading over it; the legend is a stroke key in its own 2.75rem strip under a 1px rule.

Fact box: index of lines being built and upcoming; a pick dims the others, frames the line (55 degree tilt, buildings from zoom 13) and prints its record with a 4px ink rule and figures in the display face.
Line colours only as line marks, map strokes and the bundle; stage is a stroke pattern beside its word.
stillApplies: Every rule of The Late City Edition, in both editions, including the orange bar module on section heads.
differs: The masthead band is ink, not orange, and names the site; the edition line has no back link.
Many line colours on one page, only as marks, strokes and the bundle.
Sections indent past the bundle and their 4px rule starts after it.
No lead picture, no halftone, no photos: the map is the front page's picture.
The direction brief's masthead stripe of line colours was built as the bundle instead.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Late City Edition"**

The site is a newspaper with one story. It prints in two editions: the night edition (navy paper, cream ink) when the system asks for dark, and the morning edition (warm newsprint, navy ink) otherwise. A reader can switch editions from the masthead. Every page element is a part of a paper: a masthead band, an edition line, an "Inside" index, a front page with a headline, a standfirst and a lead picture, then inside pages that each open under a heavy rule, and a corrections column at the back.

The whole identity is one orange shape, the bar module (0.5rem tall). It is the masthead band, the marker on top of every section head, the separator squares in the edition line, the progress fills, the timeline rails, the hover underline in the index and the station directory, and the casing of the route line itself. Everything else is navy, newsprint and concrete. The route is drawn after Vignelli: thick parallel strokes, one 45-degree bend, dot stations, and x spaced by true chainage. The line is not built yet, so it prints hollow (an orange casing with a paper core). The lead picture follows the Tren Urbano and MASP references: a flat-shaded isometric viaduct and train on an orange halftone field, a giant "12" painted on the road, and concrete in greys with only the train band in orange.

Density is editorial, not dashboard. Sections are solid blocks with a deep gap before the next rule. Facts sit in ruled lists and tables, not cards. Status is always a mark or a stroke pattern plus a word, never hue alone.
keyCharacteristics: One signal colour (Line 12 orange), used as bars, bands, lines and large figures, never as body text.
Heavy condensed display grotesk (Anek Latin at 75% width, weight 800), set uppercase, against a plain humanist body (Mukta).
Tabular lining numerals for every figure, date and table.
Hairline column rules and 4px heavy rules carry the structure. No shadows, no cards.
Status grammar: solid, dashed, gapped or hollow strokes; tick, ring, dashed square, crosshatch marks.
Two editions from one token set. Only the paper, ink, rule and orange-on-paper values flip.
Motion is the ride: the reader scrolls the train along the line, station by station. Without motion, the page is complete.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange is the only hue. It appears as the bar module, the route and big figures. Every other colour is paper, ink, rule or concrete.

rules.name: The Three Oranges Rule
rules.body: Pick the orange by job, not by taste: signal for fills that carry navy text, signal-graphic for shapes drawn on paper, signal-line for strokes and large figures on paper. Never set body-size text in any orange.

rules.name: The Two Editions Rule
rules.body: Every colour is written as a token that both editions define. Components never hard-code a hex; the lead picture's isometric palette is the one exception, because it always sits on the orange field.

rules.name: The Squeeze Rule
rules.body: Display type is Anek at 75% width and weight 800, uppercase, with line-height under 1. A display line at normal width or in sentence case is off-world. The one exception is the timeline event title, which drops to Mukta 700 so a long sentence stays readable.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number, date and table uses tabular lining numerals. Figures line up down a column like a stock page.

rules.name: The Balanced Head Rule
rules.body: Headings balance their lines; paragraphs wrap pretty. No orphan word on a headline.

rules.name: The Edition Rule
rules.body: Structure is printed with rules, not boxes. A heavy 4px ink rule opens each section and each major block; 1px column rules separate rows. If you reach for a card, use a rule instead.

rules.name: The True Spacing Rule
rules.body: On the route, x is proportional to chainage. Stations keep their real relative spacing on the front strip and in the ride, from the same shared geometry.

rules.name: The Printed Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats above the paper. A surface is either the page, a second sheet (paper-2), or an orange band. State never adds a shadow.

rules.name: The Halftone Rule
rules.body: The dot screen (1px dots on a 6px grid) goes only on printed-picture areas. It is never a page background.

rules.name: The Named Colour Rule
rules.body: Hub. A line shows a colour only when a source names it. Otherwise it gets no bundle stroke, a Concrete map stroke and an outlined line mark. Colour never carries stage.

rules.name: The Decorative Marathi Rule
rules.body: Marathi marks are ornament beside the English, never the copy itself. They are hidden from screen readers and set in Anek Devanagari Mark (cut to its glyphs by scripts/subset-fonts.py; rerun it when a mark changes).

rules.name: The Text Fallback Rule
rules.body: Hub. The map is never the only record. Every line, stage and figure on it is also in the fact box index and the register, with its grade. Without JavaScript each index entry links to its record.

rules.name: The Bundle Order Rule
rules.body: Hub. One stroke per primary line, in network.json order (line-number order). A branch (2A and 2B, 7A, 12A) shares its primary line's stroke, and each colour appears once (Line 12 repeats Line 5's orange, so it adds none). Today 8 strokes, Lines 1 to 8: blue, yellow, aqua, green, orange, pink, red, gold. Never reorder by hue or pick a colour by taste.

rules.name: The Fold Rule
rules.body: Hub. The front ends at the fold on a desktop screen: height max(30rem, 100svh - 22rem), from the screen, never from its content.

dos: **Do** build every new accent from the bar module: a 0.5rem hard-edged orange rectangle, or a multiple of it (1rem for progress bars).
**Do** open every section with a 4px ink rule and a section head of bar, uppercase name and standfirst.
**Do** pick the orange by job: signal under navy text, signal-graphic for shapes on paper, signal-line for strokes and large figures.
**Do** draw status as a mark or stroke pattern plus a word: solid, gapped, dashed or hollow; tick, ring, dashed square, crosshatch.
**Do** set every figure in tabular lining numerals, and give it a grade mark and a source link.
**Do** keep superseded figures on the page, struck through in Orange Ink.
**Do** write colours as tokens that both editions define, so the night and morning editions stay in step.
**Do** keep every section fully readable with motion off.
**Do** draw stage on the hub's map, legend, index and register as a stroke pattern beside its word, and show a line's colour only when a source names it.
**Do** keep a grade mark after every figure in the hub's fact box and register.
**Do** keep Marathi marks decorative: `lang="mr"`, `aria-hidden`, Anek Devanagari Mark.

**Do** compute the hub's bundle from network.json (width, bend, stops, as desktop px times --k): one 4px stroke per primary line colour on a 6px pitch, branches sharing their primary's stroke, each colour once.
donts: **Don't** add drop shadows, floating cards or glass panels. The paper is flat.
**Don't** introduce a second accent hue. Status, category and emphasis use orange, ink, rule and concrete only.
**Don't** set body-size text in any orange; Orange Ink is 4.06:1 on morning paper.
**Don't** put the halftone screen on a page background; it belongs to printed pictures.
**Don't** set display type at normal width, in a light weight, or in sentence case.
**Don't** round the bar module or the rules. Radius belongs to dots, lines, controls and pills only.
**Don't** use a small uppercase tracked label above a heading as a kicker. Labels name data and sit beside or under it.
**Don't** add cards, drop shadows, glow or glass on the hub; the street map's tilt and buildings are its only depth.
**Don't** make the hub's map the only record; every line stays in the fact box index and the register.
**Don't** label a hub map line more than once, or add counts to the legend.
**Don't** bring back the hub's retired Mumbai Key Art devices: near-black ground, photo chapters, cover tiles, pills, scrims, rounded tiles.
